title: Customer Quote & Logo Release Process (Customer-Facing Marketing)
author: Sofia Mendes
body:
## Purpose
This page defines Redwood Inference’s standard legal process for using **customer names, logos, quotes, and performance claims** in external materials (e.g., website, case studies, PDFs, sales decks, press releases, social posts, events).

The goal is to move quickly **without creating NDA/MSA conflicts** or publishing claims we cannot substantiate.

> Scope: Customer-facing marketing only. Product documentation that references customers (even indirectly) must follow this process if it includes a customer name/logo/quote or identifiable architecture details.

## Definitions (what requires a release)
A **release is required** before publishing any of the following externally:
- Customer **logo** or company name used as a “customer” or “trusted by” statement.
- Direct **quotes** from customer employees (including paraphrases that are clearly attributable).
- Named **case studies** (web or PDF) and any customer-specific success story.
- Customer-identifying **architecture diagrams** (even without a logo) if the customer could reasonably be identified.
- Any **quantified outcomes** tied to the customer (latency, cost/token, error rate, throughput, uptime) unless explicitly approved as part of a release.

A release is **not required** for:
- Completely anonymized aggregate statements that are not customer-identifying (e.g., “some customers reduced p95 latency by 30–50%” without naming and without unique details), provided the claim is approved via Marketing + Legal claims review.

## Roles and responsibilities
- **Marketing (Program Owner):** Camila Reyes
  - Owns the asset, ensures intake is complete, routes for approvals.
- **Product Marketing (Messaging/Claims):** Soojin Lee
  - Ensures claims are consistent with current capabilities and do not overpromise.
- **Legal (Primary):** Sofia Mendes
  - Reviews NDA/MSA constraints, drafts/negotiates release terms, manages redlines.
- **General Counsel (Escalations):** Michael Grant
  - Handles high-risk accounts, non-standard terms, or disputes.
- **Security/Compliance Review (as needed):** Naomi Feldman
  - Reviews security language, architecture detail sensitivity, regulated workload constraints.

## Standard workflow (end-to-end)
### 1) Intake (Marketing)
Marketing must open a release request with the following minimum information:
- Customer legal entity name (and DBA, if applicable)
- Primary customer contact(s) and approver(s)
- Asset type(s): logo on website, quote, case study, press release, event, social, partner co-marketing
- Intended publication channels (website, PDF, blog, marketplace listing, social, email, paid ads)
- Draft text for:
  - Quotes (exact wording)
  - Claims (metrics + timeframe + measurement method)
  - Any security/compliance statements
- Any diagrams/screenshots planned for publication
- Target publish date and any partner dependencies

**Do not send a release form to a customer** until Legal confirms the correct template and any MSA/NDA constraints.

### 2) Contract check (Legal)
Legal reviews the customer’s:
- NDA(s) and confidentiality provisions
- MSA / order form terms (publicity clause, IP, restrictions)
- Any prior approvals or marketing addenda

Outcomes:
- **Use standard release form** (preferred)
- **Use customer-provided form** (acceptable with review)
- **No release possible** (must anonymize or remove customer-identifying content)

### 3) Draft release package (Legal + Marketing)
Legal selects the appropriate standard language option (see “Release language options”). Marketing confirms:
- Final asset list and channels
- Exact quote(s), name/title, and attribution format
- Approved claims list (metrics and caveats)

### 4) Customer review and redlines (Legal)
- Legal is the single thread owner for negotiating legal terms.
- Marketing may join for context, but **Legal sends the final “approved to sign” form**.

### 5) Signature + storage
- Acceptable signatures: DocuSign, Adobe Sign, or email approval from an authorized approver (Legal must confirm authority).
- Store artifacts in the designated internal folder and link the final release to the program tracker.

### 6) Pre-publish verification (Marketing)
Before publishing, Marketing confirms:
- The content matches the signed release (no quote drift).
- Any metrics are consistent with the approved claim language and time windows.
- Security-sensitive details have been removed if required.

### 7) Post-publish change control
If any of the following change, the release must be updated or re-approved:
- New channels (e.g., adding paid ads, adding press release, adding marketplace listing)
- New quotes, new spokesperson, or new metrics
- Material change in claim magnitude or wording
- New diagram/screenshot/architecture detail not previously approved

## Release language options (standard)
Legal will choose the smallest scope that achieves business needs.

### Option A — Logo-only release (low risk; recommended for many customers)
**Permitted use:** Customer name and logo in Redwood customer lists (website + sales materials).
**Typical channels:** Website, PDF one-pagers, sales decks.
**Excludes:** Quotes, metrics, detailed architecture.

Common limitations we accept:
- “Use limited to Redwood-owned properties” (website + official decks)
- Brand guidelines compliance
- Pre-approval of first use (one-time)

### Option B — Quote + attribution release
Includes Option A plus:
- Approved quote(s) (exact language)
- Spokesperson name + title + company
- Approved context (e.g., “about Redwood Dedicated,” “about VPC deployment”)

Recommended requirements:
- Quote list is attached/inline (to prevent ambiguity)
- Customer may request removal if spokesperson leaves the company (reasonable timeframe)

### Option C — Case study release (named; higher scrutiny)
Includes Options A and B plus:
- Rights to publish a named case study (web + PDF)
- Permission to include high-level architecture diagram(s)
- Permission to include an approved list of measurable outcomes

Case study releases should:
- Enumerate approved claims (metrics) and the measurement window
- Include confidentiality-safe constraints (e.g., “deployed in customer VPC”) without exposing sensitive configurations
- Include explicit publication channels and permitted derivative uses (e.g., excerpts in decks)

### Option D — Press/partner co-marketing (highest scrutiny)
Includes any of the above plus:
- Press release distribution
- Partner marketplace listing co-marketing
- Event announcements

These require tighter controls:
- Final copy approval by customer (and partner, if applicable)
- A single “source of truth” version control process (Marketing owns content; Legal confirms release scope)

## Handling NDAs and MSAs (common scenarios)
### Scenario 1: NDA prohibits disclosure of relationship
If the NDA/MSA prohibits acknowledging the relationship:
- We cannot use name/logo/quote.
- Alternatives:
  - Anonymized case study (“Top 5 US insurer…”) if allowed
  - Aggregate claims not attributable to the customer

Escalate to GC if Sales requests an exception.

### Scenario 2: MSA has a publicity clause
Many MSAs require customer approval for any public use of brand/name.
- The release form functions as that written approval.
- Ensure the release does not conflict with the MSA’s notice or approval requirements.

### Scenario 3: Customer provides their own release form
Acceptable if:
- Scope is clear (channels, term, withdrawal)
- It does not add unacceptable obligations (see “Redline guidance”)

### Scenario 4: Regulated workload / security constraints
If the customer is in healthcare, finance, insurance, government, or otherwise regulated:
- Avoid publishing detailed security architecture, data flows, retention windows, region lists, or vendor names that increase risk.
- Include “sanitized architecture diagram” language if needed.
- Route through Security/Compliance review.

## Redline guidance (what we typically accept vs. push back on)
### Generally acceptable redlines
- Require brand guidelines compliance
- Limit channels to specific Redwood-owned properties
- One-time pre-approval of first use (or approval per asset)
- Reasonable withdrawal right (see below)

### Redlines to push back on (requires Legal review)
- Unlimited indemnities from Redwood for marketing use
- Broad IP assignment or ownership of Redwood materials
- Approval rights that effectively block any update indefinitely (e.g., “customer may withhold approval in sole discretion” without timelines)
- Confidentiality clauses that prohibit Redwood from keeping internal copies of the approved asset

### Withdrawal / termination language (preferred)
We prefer:
- Customer may withdraw permission with **written notice**
- Redwood will remove from future materials within **30–60 days**
- No obligation to recall already distributed materials (e.g., previously printed decks), but we stop further distribution

## Claims, metrics, and proof requirements (legal + messaging)
When a case study or quote includes quantified outcomes:
- The exact metric statements must be listed in the release (or attached as an exhibit).
- Include the measurement window and the qualifier (e.g., “in production,” “during a 30-day period,” “for this workload shape”).
- Avoid absolute guarantees (“always,” “eliminated all incidents”). Use accurate, bounded language.

Examples of acceptable phrasing:
- “Reduced p95 latency by 38% on their support-agent chat workload (30-day production window).”
- “Lowered cost per resolved ticket by ~22% after enabling caching and batching recommendations.”
- “Improved error rate from 1.4% to 0.3% by configuring fallback policies and rate limits.”

Examples of wording that requires revision:
- “Guaranteed sub-200ms latency.”
- “SOC 2 compliant deployment” (use “supports SOC 2-aligned controls” or “used in a SOC 2 environment,” depending on facts).

## Escalation criteria (to General Counsel)
Escalate to **Michael Grant (GC)** when any of the following are true:
- Customer is flagged as sensitive (government, defense, critical infrastructure, highly regulated) or has strict publicity constraints
- Customer requests non-standard liability, indemnity, or IP terms
- Customer’s legal team disputes NDA/MSA interpretation
- The asset is a press release or partner co-marketing announcement with tight timelines
- The case study includes unusually detailed architecture/security content
- Any request to publish despite contractual restrictions

## SLA and planning guidance
Typical turnaround times (business days):
- Intake completeness check (Marketing): 1–2
- Contract check + select release option (Legal): 2–4
- Standard release review with minimal redlines: 5–10 (depends on customer)
- Customer-provided form or heavy redlines: 10–20+

Plan for additional time if:
- Multiple approver groups exist on the customer side (Comms + Legal + Security)
- Metrics require validation or incident review before publication

## Templates and required artifacts
Use the standard template unless Legal approves otherwise:
- **Customer Quote/Logo Release Form Template** (Confluence template)

Artifacts to store for every approval:
- Final signed release (PDF or signed email thread)
- Final approved quote(s) and attribution block
- Final approved claims list (metrics + caveats)
- Final approved case study/PDF copy (if applicable)
- Any customer brand guidelines supplied

## FAQ
**Q: Can Sales use a customer logo in a private pitch deck without a release?**
A: No. External-facing includes prospect-facing sales materials. Use anonymized references until a release is signed.

**Q: Can we publish an anonymized case study without a release?**
A: Sometimes. Legal must confirm that the anonymized story cannot reasonably identify the customer and does not violate NDA/MSA.

**Q: If the customer approved a quote last year, can we reuse it?**
A: Only if the prior release explicitly permits reuse for the current channels and the quote/attribution is unchanged.

## Contact
For release requests, route through Legal (Sofia Mendes). For escalations or urgent deal deadlines, contact Michael Grant (GC) and include Marketing (Camila Reyes) on the thread.
